value: (f+g)(x) = x + |x| = 2x for x >= 0, and 0 for x < 0
why: For x >= 0, |x| = x so x + |x| = 2x; for x < 0, |x| = -x so x + |x| = 0. Checked at x = -5, -1, -1/2, 0, 1/2, 1, 5: option C matches every point, B fails at every negative x, D fails at every positive x.

value: log(a+2b) = log(4*sqrt(ab)) = (1/2)(log a + log b + 4 log 2)
why: (a+2b)^2 = a^2 + 4ab + 4b^2 = 12ab + 4ab = 16ab, so a+2b = 4 sqrt(ab) and log(a+2b) = 2 log 2 + (1/2)(log a + log b), which is exactly option C. Verified on both roots a = 2b(3 +/- 2 sqrt 2) of the constraint at b = 1, 3 and 7/5: C holds at all three, and option D holds ONLY at b = 1 (a coincidence, since it needs ab-vs-a/b to agree there), so D is a near-miss distractor and not equivalent.

value: Statement I true and Statement II true
why: I: A^T = -A gives (A^2)^T = (A^T)^2 = (-A)^2 = A^2, so A^2 is symmetric (confirmed on a general 3x3 skew matrix). II: every diagonal entry satisfies a_ii = -a_ii so a_ii = 0 and the trace is zero for skew-symmetric matrices of ANY order, hence in particular for odd order the statement is true (note the classic odd-order result about the DETERMINANT is a different claim; the trace claim as printed is still true).

"non-zero positive integers" means x, y >= 1, so enumerating x + y <= 4 gives exactly 6 ordered pairs (brute-forced). If zero were allowed the count would be 15, which matches no option, so the intended reading is confirmed by the option set.

A^k = [[1,k],[0,1]], so the sum over k = 1..n-1 is [[n-1, (1+2+...+(n-1))],[0, n-1]] = [[n-1, n(n-1)/2],[0, n-1]]. Computed the actual matrix sum for n = 2,3,4,5,7 and compared against all four options: only C matches at every n (A has diagonal n instead of n-1; B and D have a wrong 1 in the lower-left).

C is opposite c = 2, so cos C = (16 + 9 - 4)/(2*4*3) = 21/24 = 7/8; cos 3C = 4(7/8)^3 - 3(7/8) = 343/128 - 336/128 = 7/128. Confirmed independently by evaluating cos(3 arccos(7/8)) symbolically, and the triangle 4,3,2 is valid.

value: x = 30 degrees (pi/6), where sqrt(3) cos x + sin x attains its maximum value 2
why: sqrt(3) cos x + sin x = 2 cos(x - 30 deg), maximised when x = 30 deg. Solving the derivative gives the single critical point pi/6, and evaluating the expression at the four offered angles gives 2.000 (30), 1.932 (45), 1.732 (60), 1.000 (90) - so 30 degrees is the unique maximiser among the options.

value: P(A) = 1/5 (the system also admits P(A) = 3/5, but only 1/5 appears among the options)
why: Independence gives p(1-q) = 3/25 and (1-p)q = 8/25; subtracting yields q = p + 1/5, leading to 25p^2 - 20p + 3 = 0 with roots p = 1/5 (q = 2/5) and p = 3/5 (q = 4/5). Both are valid probability pairs and both satisfy the two given constraints exactly, which is why the stem says "could be"; of the options only 1/5 is a possible P(A) (4/5 is the value of P(B) in the second solution, not P(A)).

With n = 16 and a fair coin the stated condition P(7 heads) = P(9 heads) is automatically satisfied (C(16,7) = C(16,9) = 11440), so it is only a consistency check. P(X=3) = 560/2^16, and 560 = 16 * 35 so this reduces exactly to 35/2^12, which is option A; the other three options evaluate to 35/65536, 1/256 and 7/1024, none equal to 35/4096.

A sphere touching a plane has radius equal to the distance from its centre to the plane: |6(1) - 3(-2) + 2(3) - 4| / sqrt(36+9+4) = 14/7 = 2, giving diameter 4. All arithmetic exact (the denominator sqrt(49) = 7 is exact, so no rounding is involved).

value: f'(x) = -(x+2)/(x+1)^2 < 0 for all x > 0, so f is decreasing
why: f'(x) = -1/(x+1)^2 - 1/(1+x) = -(x+2)/(x+1)^2. For x > 0 the numerator -(x+2) is strictly negative and the denominator is strictly positive, so f' < 0 on the whole domain, i.e. f is strictly decreasing (spot-checked at x = 0.001, 1, 10, 1000, all negative). There is no sign change, so C and D are ruled out.

np = 4 and npq = 3 give q = 3/4, p = 1/4, n = 16 (unique solution), so P(X=1) = C(16,1)(1/4)(3/4)^15 = 4(3/4)^15. Option A is 16(3/4)^15, exactly 4 times too large (the classic "dropped the factor p" distractor, 0.2138 vs 0.0535); option B is 4(1/4)^15 ~= 3.7e-9; option C is the parameter pair "n=16, p=1/4", which is a true statement but is not a value of P(X=1) and does not answer the question asked. Hence "None of these" is correct as printed. Flagging that the option set looks mangled - option C answers a different question - so the source may have intended 4(3/4)^15 as an option.

Antiderivative of (1-x)^9 is -(1-x)^10/10, so the definite integral from 0 to 1 is 0 - (-1/10) = 1/10 (confirmed symbolically). Equivalently substituting u = 1-x gives the integral of u^9 from 0 to 1.

value: Zero - the collinearity conditions are mutually inconsistent, so no real k works
why: Collinearity of P(k,1,3), Q(1,-2,k+1), R(15,2,-4) requires (R-P) x (Q-P) = 0. The cross product is (k-23, k^2-10k+23, 4k-46): its components vanish at k = 23, at k = 5 +/- sqrt 2, and at k = 23/2 respectively, and the simultaneous system has no solution. No degenerate escape either - P, Q, R can never coincide pairwise for any k (the y-coordinates 1, -2, 2 already forbid it).

(sin x + cos x)^2 = 1 + sin 2x, and on [0, pi/2] sin x + cos x >= 1 > 0 so sqrt(1 + sin 2x) = sin x + cos x; the integrand therefore reduces exactly to sin x + cos x, whose integral over [0, pi/2] is [sin x - cos x] = 1 - (-1) = 2. Confirmed by direct numerical evaluation of the original unsimplified integrand to 30 digits: 2.00000000000000.
